theater: 科林斯灣與薩羅尼科斯灣

battle.name: 第一次伯羅奔尼撒戰爭
battle.theater: 科林斯灣與薩羅尼科斯灣
battle.brief: 公元前460年至445年，雅典聯盟與斯巴達聯盟在科林斯灣與薩羅尼科斯灣開戰。雅典以海軍遊擊伯羅奔尼撒沿岸，奪取奧厄尼亞達等海灣要點，在玻俄提亞與斯巴達方陣交鋒，卻在塔納格拉一度失利；公元前446/5年雙方以三十年和約收場。卡面的斯巴達長矛正是這場戰爭裡雙方重裝步兵方陣的核心兵器。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前460年開打、到公元前446/5年才以和約收場的第一次伯羅奔尼撒戰爭，交戰的兩大系統是雅典海帝國與斯巴達陸權聯盟。雅典一方以德摩斯提尼聯盟（提洛同盟）為框架：核心是雅典城邦的公民軍，據當時估算可徵集的公民重裝步兵約三千至四千人，另有外邦人組成的同盟軍，以及各島、各城的駐防分遣隊；作戰指揮由十位將軍（strategoi）輪值，實務上多由同一批人連任，戰略決策則握在五百人議事會與公民大會手中，伯羅克利斯一系在戰爭大部分時間裡影響最大。斯巴達一方是伯羅奔尼撒同盟：以斯巴達公民兵為骨幹，另有科林斯、玻俄提亞諸邦（底比斯、坦納格拉）、西基昂、佩累涅、埃皮達魯斯、特洛伊曾、哈利埃斯，以及一部分梅加拉人的兵力；科林斯城邦還帶來海軍技術與克里特、埃吉納方面的用兵傳統。斯巴達的實際決策權在三十人長老會與五名監察官手上，兩位國王各自率領王族部隊，盟軍則須在斯巴達召開會議才能決定出兵，因此調動遲緩而各懷心思。雅典靠同盟貢金（phoros）與愛琴海航線維持這場戰爭，斯巴達靠伯羅奔尼撒的陸軍與聯盟分攤軍費。雙方真正的矛盾，是愛琴海制海權與科林斯灣陸路通道之爭。
countriesEn: This war was the First Peloponnesian War, which opened in 460 BC and was not closed by a treaty until 446/5 BC, and the two systems arrayed against each other were the maritime empire of Athens and the land power of the Spartan alliance. On the Athenian side the frame was the Delian League: the core was the citizen army of the city of Athens, estimated at three to four thousand hoplites liable to serve, supplemented by troops of the subject states and by garrison detachments drawn from the islands and the dependent cities. Command at the level of operations lay with a board of ten strategoi, in practice the same men holding the post year after year, while the real decisions of policy rested with the Council of Five Hundred and the Assembly, and the influence of Pericles' circle was dominant for most of the war. The Spartan side was the Peloponnesian League: the backbone was the Spartan citizen force, with contingents from Corinth, the Boeotian cities such as Thebes and Tanagra, Sicyon, Pellene, Epidaurus, Troezen, Halieis and a part of the Megarians; Corinth also brought naval technique and the traditions of fighting in the pay of Crete and Aegina. Decision-making at Sparta lay with the Council of Thirty and the five ephors, while the two kings commanded their separate royal contingents, and the allies could only be brought to the field by a congress held at Sparta, so mobilisation was slow and every member pulled in its own direction. Athens paid for the war with the phoros of its allies and the shipping lanes of the Aegean, and Sparta with the hoplite armies of the Peloponnese and a levy shared among the allies. The real quarrel between them was the struggle between command of the Aegean sea and control of the land route through the Gulf of Corinth.
people: 這場戰爭裡真正左右走向的是雅典的伯羅克利斯。他日後那篇著名的「伯羅克利斯葬禮辭」說的正是這段經歷：雅典的強處在海軍與帝國，而這樣的帝國正是在這場戰爭的實踐中一步步撐起來的。他主持了與阿爾戈斯、曼提涅亞、埃利斯的同盟，把梅加拉爭取到雅典一方，並在遠征色薩利時吃過敗仗。戰役層面上，他兩度率軍深入：公元前457年率一千名重裝步兵與五千名投槍手入色薩利，敗於色薩利騎兵；公元前446/5年斯巴達大軍入侵阿提卡時，他在奧埃諾埃與梅托涅兩處設防而拒絕野戰，最後靠敵軍自己染疫撤退。他手下的將領各守一條戰線：托爾米德斯在科林斯灣奪取奧厄尼亞達並焚毀科林斯的萊凱烏姆船塢；彌羅尼德斯在玻俄提亞取錫斐萊、於俄厄諾弗塔大勝；提摩太在科林斯灣取得一場被修昔底德稱為「希臘人迄今為止最大海戰」的勝利；拉刻斯與卡里克勒斯遠征埃及而失敗；客蒙在色雷斯擊敗色雷斯人，又在第二次聖戰中對波斯作戰，最後陣亡於塞浦路斯，促成阿里斯提德一系所代表的與波斯之間的和約。斯巴達方面，幕後主導者是監察官與長老會；攝政普利斯托拿克斯與保桑那斯率領的入侵阿提卡大軍、尚未即位的阿基達穆斯二世，以及在坦納格拉指揮聯軍的克萊翁布羅托斯，都是決定單場戰鬥的關鍵人物。
peopleEn: The man who really shaped the course of the war was Pericles of Athens. The famous Funeral Oration that goes under his name describes precisely this experience: that the strength of Athens lay in her fleet and her empire, and that such an empire was built up step by step in the practice of this war. He managed the alliances with Argos, Mantinea and Elis, won Megara over to the Athenian side, and was beaten in the field during his expedition into Thessaly. At the level of operations he twice led an army deep inland: in 457 BC he marched into Thessaly with a thousand hoplites and five thousand javelin men and was defeated by the Thessalian cavalry; and in 446/5 BC, when a large Spartan army invaded Attica, he took up positions at Oenoe and Methone and refused a pitched battle, and in the end it was a plague in the invading host that made it withdraw. The generals under him each held a line of the theatre: Tolmides took Oeniadae in the Gulf of Corinth and burned the dockyard of Lechaeum; Myronides took Siphylae in Boeotia and won at Oenophyta; Timotheus gained in the Gulf of Corinth a victory that Thucydides called the greatest sea battle yet fought between the Greeks; Laches and Charicles were sent to Egypt and failed; Cimon beat the Thracians in Thrace and campaigned against the Persians in the Second Sacred War, and was killed in Cyprus, opening the way to the peace with Persia represented by Aristides. On the Spartan side the men behind the scenes were the ephors and the Council of Thirty; the invading army into Attica led by the regent Pleistoanax and Pausanias, the future king Archidamus II, and Cleombrotus who commanded the allied army at Tanagra, were the figures who decided individual battles.
kits: 卡面上這件斯巴達長矛（多利矛）正正站在這場戰爭的中心：它是重裝步兵方陣的骨幹兵器。矛杆約兩米，上端裝葉形鐵矛頭，杆尾有一截可以插入地面的銅套（sauroter）。在塔納格拉、俄厄諾弗塔與哈利埃圖斯這些陣地上的短兵相接裡，隊形一亂，銅套插進土裡就再也拔不出來，後排便無法遞補前排，整列就這麼垮掉。方陣的重裝步兵還配備科林斯式青銅頭盔、肌甲、脛甲、大圓盾（aspis）與一柄短劍（xiphos），最後的近身肉搏仍靠短劍解決，長矛只負責把對方保持在刺擊距離之外。雅典方面的遠程與輕裝部隊包括弓箭手、持小盾的輕裝兵（peltast）、投石手與騎兵；斯巴達與科林斯則以海軍、騎兵與多利海船的運輸能力，支撐科林斯灣的爭奪。除了兵器，還有同樣決定勝負的裝備體系：雅典的三列槳船、港口船塢、連接城邦與比雷埃夫斯海港的長城構成補給線，同盟貢金從德洛斯寶庫運回雅典後，轉化為船員、槍手與僱傭兵的口糧與工資；攻城方則靠圍城、封鎖與築堡，而不是野戰衝鋒。卡面標出的公元前800年，代表的是長矛的早期形制；到了這場戰爭，標準的多利矛已是全希臘軍隊的通用裝備，兩軍的差別只在於誰能在方陣中把它舉得穩。
kitsEn: The Spartan spear on the card, the dory, stood at the very centre of this war: it was the backbone weapon of the hoplite phalanx. The shaft was about two metres long, carrying a leaf-shaped iron head at the top, and the butt ended in a bronze spike, the sauroter, that could be planted in the ground. In the close fighting on the field at Tanagra, Oenophyta and Haliartus, once the line broke the spike was driven into the earth and could not be pulled out again, the files behind could not relieve the files in front, and the whole row came apart on its own. The hoplite of the phalanx also carried a Corinthian bronze helmet, a cuirass, greaves, the great round shield, the aspis, and a short sword, the xiphos; the last killing at arm's length was still done with the sword, the spear serving only to hold the enemy at stabbing distance. On the Athenian side the ranged and light troops were archers, peltasts with their small crescent shields, slingers and cavalry; Sparta and Corinth relied on their fleets, their cavalry and the carrying capacity of dolia to sustain the struggle in the Gulf of Corinth. Beyond the weapons there was an apparatus that decided as much: the Athenian triremes, the dockyards, the Long Walls linking the city to the harbour of Piraeus formed the line of supply, and the phoros of the allies, once the treasury had been moved from Delos back to Athens, was converted into rations and wages for crews, archers and mercenaries; and the side that besieged did so by blockade, investment and fortification rather than by assault. The year 800 BC given on the card marks an early form of the spear; by the time of this war the standard dory was the common equipment of every army in Greece, and the difference between the two sides lay only in who could keep it steady inside the phalanx.
tactics: 雙方的戰術都圍繞同一個問題：誰來決定會戰的地點與時間。斯巴達聯軍的傳統打法是重裝步兵密集方陣，右翼由精銳部隊掩護，陣線保持縱深以增加前排支撐，逼近之後以推撞與刺擊把敵陣推垮；科林斯與玻俄提亞的步兵則在兩翼與後方提供縱深。公元前457年的塔納格拉之戰，聯軍正是靠方陣推進擊敗了雅典的散兵；其後的俄厄諾弗塔一役，彌羅尼德斯反過來用同樣的密集隊形打崩了玻俄提亞聯軍，說明這場戰爭裡方陣的用法是雙向的。雅典的戰略核心是不打無把握的野戰：其公民重裝步兵人數少於斯巴達，一旦在開闊地會戰必敗，所以雅典選擇以海軍遊擊、封鎖海峽、切斷敵方沿岸城市、爭取同盟，而不是在阿提卡平原迎戰斯巴達。托爾米德斯與提摩太在科林斯灣奪取海灣要塞、焚燒船塢，正是一次典型的敵後消耗；提摩太的海戰則靠三列槳船包抄、衝撞與拖曳，逼迫敵艦在狹窄海面轉向，顯示雅典的戰術核心是船而不是陣。攻城多採用圍而不攻：雅典包圍坦納格拉時並未強攻，卻在斯巴達遠征阿提卡時被迫放棄，這說明圍城補給與援軍爭奪才是真正的戰略。公元前446/5年斯巴達大軍進入阿提卡後沒有主動求戰，雅典以海軍與城牆應對，最後靠敵軍疫病自行退兵。
tacticsEn: The tactics of both sides turned on the same question: who would decide the place and the moment of the battle. The traditional method of the Spartan alliance was a dense phalanx of hoplites with the right wing covered by the picked troops, the line kept deep so that the front rank had support, and the advance made by shoving and stabbing until the opposing line collapsed; the hoplites of Corinth and Boeotia supplied the depth on the wings and in the rear. In the battle of Tanagra in 457 BC it was the advance of the phalanx that broke the disordered Athenians; at Oenophyta in the same year Myronides turned the same dense formation against the Boeotian allies and shattered them, which shows that the phalanx worked in both directions in this war. The core of Athenian strategy was to refuse any pitched battle it could not win: its citizen hoplites were fewer than Sparta's and would necessarily lose a battle fought in the open, so Athens chose to raid by sea, close the straits, cut the enemy's coastal cities off and win over allies instead of meeting the Spartans on the plains of Attica. Tolmides' and Timotheus' seizures of the ports of the Gulf of Corinth and the burning of the dockyards were typical attacks on the enemy's rear; the sea battle won by Timotheus was fought by outflanking with triremes, ramming and towing, forcing the enemy to row round in a narrow space, which shows that the Athenian centre of gravity was the ship and not the line. Besieging was generally done by investment rather than assault: the Athenians did not storm Tanagra when they invested it, and were forced to abandon the investment when Sparta invaded Attica, which shows that the real strategic question was supply during a siege and the contest for reinforcements. When the Spartan army entered Attica in 446/5 BC it did not seek a battle, and Athens answered with its fleet and its walls, until the plague in the enemy host made it withdraw on its own.
data: 可核的數字不多，但足以描出戰爭的規模。戰爭慣例起訖於公元前460年至445年，前段是斯巴達與盟邦之間的公開衝突，後段才是雅典與其同盟之間的戰爭，最終以三十年和約收束；具體的開戰月份無可靠記載，卡面標為四月，取的是開戰當年春夏之際、雅典開始在科林斯灣出手的通說。公元前460年，雅典在科林斯灣奪取奧厄尼亞達並焚毀萊凱烏姆的科林斯船塢，這是本役第一次大規模的兩棲作戰。公元前457年，伯羅克利斯率一千重裝步兵與五千投槍手遠征色薩利，這個兵力數字出自修昔底德。公元前454/3年赴埃及的遠征軍是全役最大的一次出兵：二百艘三列槳船、一萬名重裝步兵、一千名弓箭手（其中含五百名投槍手），結果在尼羅河三角洲一役失利，損失數十艘船，帝國財政亦因此第一次吃緊，德洛斯寶庫則早在數年前已運回雅典。公元前451年客蒙自同盟各城徵得四千名重裝步兵（其中雅典出二千），在色雷斯擊敗色雷斯人；同年伯羅克利斯以一百艘三列槳船巡行黑海，取辛諾普並遠征克里米亞。公元前448/7年平定歐玻亞時，伯羅克利斯率一百艘三列槳船與五千重裝步兵。公元前446/5年斯巴達入侵阿提卡的兵力，修昔底德沒有留下數字，後世多推估重裝步兵在三萬上下，屬估算而非確錄。單艘三列槳船約長三十七米、需一百七十名槳手，可載重裝步兵五十人上下；雅典同盟的年貢金在戰爭前中期約在四百至六百塔蘭特之間浮動。距離方面，雅典至科林斯陸路約一百五十公里，而海軍可由比雷埃夫斯直抵萊凱烏姆，航程與陸路相差無幾。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are not many, but they are enough to show the scale of the war. The war is conventionally dated from 460 to 445 BC: an open clash between Sparta and its allies in the earlier phase, and a war between Athens and its allies in the later one, closed at last by the Thirty Years' Peace; no reliable record gives the exact month in which the war began, and the card gives April, which takes the usual view that hostilities opened in the spring and early summer of 460 BC when Athens first took the offensive in the Gulf of Corinth. In 460 BC the Athenians took Oeniadae in the Gulf and burned the Corinthian dockyard at Lechaeum, the first large amphibious operation of the war. In 457 BC Pericles marched into Thessaly with a thousand hoplites and five thousand javelin men, and that figure for the strength of the force comes from Thucydides. The expedition to Egypt in 454/3 BC was the largest deployment of the whole war: two hundred triremes, ten thousand hoplites and a thousand archers, of whom five hundred were peltasts; it ended in defeat in the Nile delta with the loss of several tens of ships, and the finances of the empire felt the strain for the first time, the treasury at Delos having been moved back to Athens some years earlier. In 451 BC Cimon took four thousand hoplites from the cities of the alliance, two thousand of them from Athens, and beat the Thracians in Thrace; in the same year Pericles cruised the Black Sea with a hundred triremes, took Sinope and carried the war as far as the Crimea. When Euboea was brought to terms in 448/7 BC, Pericles used a hundred triremes and five thousand hoplites. For the Spartan invasion of Attica in 446/5 BC Thucydides left no figures, and later estimates of around thirty thousand hoplites are computations rather than records. A single trireme was about thirty-seven metres long, needed about one hundred and seventy rowers, and could carry some fifty hoplites; the annual tribute of the Athenian alliance fluctuated between roughly four hundred and six hundred talents in the middle years before the war. As for distance, the road from Athens to Corinth is about one hundred and fifty kilometres, and the fleet could run from Piraeus straight to Lechaeum, so the sea route and the land route were of comparable length.
cause: 打起來的直接契機，是科林斯與雅典在科林斯灣的殖民地與商路爭端。科林斯是希臘本土最老的商業城邦之一，握有地峽與萊凱烏姆的船塢；雅典則在德洛斯同盟的框架下把勢力伸向科林斯灣。波特伊達是科林斯的殖民地卻又受雅典支配，公元前460年它投向科林斯，兩軍在城郊交鋒，雅典隨後以武力迫其歸附，而這些越海「懲罰」行動正是斯巴達最忌諱的越界行為。更深一層看，第一次伯羅奔尼撒戰爭的根子，是希臘世界的權力結構在波斯戰爭之後被徹底改寫：雅典以帝國姿態掌握愛琴海與黑海航路，斯巴達仍守著伯羅奔尼撒的陸權秩序，兩套體系不可能同時成立。伯羅克利斯一系的策略很清楚——把海灣的出入口變成雅典的城邑與屏障；縱觀戰爭全期，奧厄尼亞達的歸順、辛諾普的取下、歐玻亞的整頓、刻索尼索斯的設防，都是這條擴張線上的節點。斯巴達必須阻止這種局面固定下來，因為一旦雅典的帝國把科林斯灣與黑海連成一條不受斯巴達制約的通路，伯羅奔尼撒的農業區就再也沒有安全的外銷市場。外交層面還有一層原因：斯巴達聯盟內部對雅典的擴張本來意見分歧，盟軍會議長期議而不決，這場戰爭同時也是斯巴達用一次有限度的戰爭去鞏固聯盟內部團結的手段。
causeEn: The immediate occasion for the fighting was the quarrel between Corinth and Athens over colonies and trade routes in the Gulf of Corinth. Corinth was one of the oldest trading cities of the Greek mainland and held the isthmus and the dockyard of Lechaeum, while Athens, within the framework of the Delian League, was extending her power into the Gulf. Potidaea was a Corinthian colony yet subject to Athens, and in 460 BC it went over to Corinth; the two sides fought outside the town, and Athens then used force to bring it back under her control, and it was precisely this kind of punitive expedition across the sea that Sparta found intolerable. At a deeper level the root of the First Peloponnesian War lay in the fact that the power structure of the Greek world had been completely rewritten after the Persian Wars: Athens held the lanes of the Aegean and the Black Sea as an empire, while Sparta still guarded the land order of the Peloponnese, and the two systems could not both stand. The strategy of Pericles' circle was plain enough, to turn the entrances of the gulfs into Athenian towns and barriers; taken one after another across the whole war, the submission of Oeniadae, the taking of Sinope, the settlement of Euboea and the fortification of the Chersonese were all stations on that line of expansion. Sparta had to prevent that situation from hardening, for once an Athenian empire joined the Gulf of Corinth to the Black Sea by a route the Spartans could not control, the agricultural districts of the Peloponnese would have no secure market for their produce. There is also a diplomatic layer to it: the Spartan alliance was itself divided over Athenian expansion, the congress of the allies deliberated for a long time without result, and the war was in part the means by which Sparta used a limited conflict to hold its own alliance together.
impact: 第一次伯羅奔尼撒戰爭沒有寫下驚天動地的勝負，卻把希臘世界的地圖改了。和平條約裡雅典表面上退出了玻俄提亞，交還了錫斐萊、凱羅涅與忒斯庇亞的平原，收回地盤看似吃虧；但這場戰爭真正的果實不必靠條約去拿：科林斯灣的兩端落進了雅典手中，歐玻亞及其城邦被整頓成附庸，色雷斯的刻索尼索斯得到設防與移民，黑海航線的兩端也進入雅典的視野。雅典帝國的財政因為遠征埃及的失敗而第一次被重估，德洛斯寶庫此前已移回雅典，貢金成為帝國運轉的血液，後來兩次伯羅奔尼撒戰爭的勝負歸根結柢是誰能撐住這筆開支。另一面，斯巴達的處境變壞了：它在戰爭中暴露了大軍遠征本土作戰的脆弱，主力一旦離境，補給、疫病與同盟不齊三項缺口就一起爆開，人口結構偏重步兵的斯巴達城邦其實極不擅長打持久戰。希臘世界從此被固定成兩大陣營的格局，即德摩斯提尼聯盟對伯羅奔尼撒同盟、雅典對斯巴達。這種對立在思想層面也被確立：智者學派、悲劇與修辭在同一個歷史背景下成熟，希臘人第一次在語言裡記錄並思考權力與帝國這件事。最後，和約沒有解決任何根本爭端，反而把兩軍之間的仇恨延後十五年爆發，這就是第二次伯羅奔尼撒戰爭的來歷。
impactEn: The First Peloponnesian War produced no spectacular victory, but it redrew the map of the Greek world. In the peace settlement Athens apparently conceded by withdrawing from Boeotia and giving up Siphylae, Chaeronea and the plain of Thespiae, and by the terms of the treaty it looked as though it had lost ground; but the real fruits of the war were not things a treaty had to grant: both ends of the Gulf of Corinth fell into Athenian hands, Euboea and its cities were reorganised as dependencies, the Thracian Chersonese was fortified and settled with colonists, and both ends of the Black Sea route came within Athenian view. The finances of the Athenian empire were reassessed for the first time because of the failure in Egypt, the treasury at Delos having been moved back to Athens some years before, and the tribute became the blood of the empire; the issue of the two later Peloponnesian wars came down in the end to who could keep that spending going. On the other side the Spartan position grew worse: the war exposed how fragile a mass army was when it campaigned deep into enemy territory, for once the main body left home, the three gaps of supply, disease and an alliance that did not move in step all opened at once, and a Spartan polis whose population leaned on infantry was in fact poor at waging a long war. The Greek world was now fixed into the shape of two blocs, the Delian League against the Peloponnesian League, Athens against Sparta. That opposition was fixed in the realm of thought as well: the sophists, the tragedies and the rhetoric of the age matured against the same historical background, and for the first time the Greeks recorded and thought in words about power and empire. In the end the peace settled no fundamental quarrel; it merely deferred the hatred between the two sides by fifteen years, and that deferral is the origin of the Second Peloponnesian War.
result: 公元前446/5年（亦有史家繫於445/4年），雅典與斯巴達在斯巴達召開的會議上訂下「三十年和約」：斯巴達保證不攻擊德摩斯提尼聯盟各城，雅典則撤出玻俄提亞，把佩拉特、埃萊亞等自己扶植的政權交還原狀，雙方各守現有疆界，互不賠償。單看條款是平手，單看地圖是斯巴達的小勝，雅典失去了在陸地上的支點。但就長期的力量對比而言，這份和約其實是雅典的收穫：海軍的制海權沒有被條約限制，雅典的同盟體系完好無損，同盟貢金照收，黑海與科林斯灣的航線照走，帝國機器在戰後升級得更完整；斯巴達則以一次入侵失敗和一次疫病退兵，證明自己沒有能力用遠征解決問題。戰爭的最後一場衝突因此充滿反諷：公元前446/5年斯巴達傾巢出動，兵臨奧埃諾埃，雅典的答案是按兵不動、不予野戰，任由疫病在敵軍中流行，最後敵軍自行撤回，雅典再在談判桌上拿回條款應得的東西。全役的勝負其實早在別處分出：這是一場以海軍與外交手段取勝的戰爭，斯巴達在方陣裡再強，也沒有艦隊去爭奪科林斯灣的兩端。
resultEn: In 446/5 BC, though some historians place it in 445/4 BC, Athens and Sparta concluded the Thirty Years' Peace at a congress held at Sparta: Sparta guaranteed that it would not attack the cities of the Delian League, and Athens withdrew from Boeotia and handed back the governments it had set up at places such as Plataea and Eleusis, each side keeping its existing borders and neither paying compensation. By the letter of the terms it was a draw, and by the map it was a small Spartan victory, for Athens lost its footholds on land. But in the long run the balance of power, this peace was in fact an Athenian gain: naval command of the sea was not restricted by the treaty, the Athenian alliance came through it undamaged, the tribute went on being paid, the lanes of the Black Sea and the Gulf of Corinth stayed open, and the imperial machine was upgraded into a more complete shape after the war; while Sparta, after a failed invasion and a retreat caused by disease, had proved that it could not solve problems by campaigning far afield. The last engagement of the war is therefore full of irony: in 446/5 BC Sparta emptied the city into the field and stood before Oenoe, and the Athenian answer was to hold still and refuse a battle, letting the plague run in the enemy host until it withdrew of its own accord, after which Athens recovered on the negotiating table exactly what the terms had owed it. The verdict of the whole war was in fact settled elsewhere: this was a war won by sea power and diplomacy, and however strong the Spartan phalanx was, Sparta had no fleet with which to contest the two ends of the Gulf of Corinth.
